newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B shares soar in active trading.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B shares soar in active trading.

text.p: Shanghai B shares soared on Monday in active trading on a rise in the Shenzhen B share market and rumours of official steps to boost the B markets, with overseas investors seen buying selective stocks, brokers said.
The index rose 1.988 points or 3.92 percent to 52.662 points, on volume of 26.4 million shares worth $9.4 million. Of 42 B shares, 40 traded, with 30 up, three flat and seven down.

Brokers said the recent bullish Shenzhen B share market had boosted the Shanghai market, helped by rumours that the authorities would take measures to boost the B share markets, which had also encouraged overseas investors to buy.
"Obviously fresh capital has flown into the market, with market sentiment improving thanks to the bullish Shenzhen B share market," one broker said.
"The index will consolidate tomorrow on profit-taking expected after today's rise but is likely to find support from institutions at the 52-point level," another broker said.

Newcomer Huangshan Tourism was the star on the most active follow-up buying after making a strong debut, but its further rise will be limited, brokers said. It surged $0.042 or 15.10 percent to $0.320, on volume of 3.6 million shares.
Shanghai Tyre Rubber followed on buying from institutions who held large positions, jumping $0.046 or 13.85 percent to $0.378, on volume of 612,000 shares.

Market barometer Shanghai Lujiazui Finance & Trade Zone set a record high of $1.030, on expectations of more preferential policies in the zone, brokers said. It ended up $0.062 or 6.40 percent to 1.030, on volume of 1.5 million shares.
Shanghai's A share index rose sharply, with market sentiment recovering a little after falls since last Thursday, brokers said.

The A index ended up 25.652 points or 2.56 percent to 1025.760 points, on volume of 495.1 million shares worth 4.6 billion yuan. The SSE 30 blue-chip index rose 41.864 points or 1.73 percent to 2467.705 points.
Sichuan Electric was the star on speculative buying, up 2.18 yuan or 20.37 percent to 12.88 yuan, on volume of 1.9 million shares.
